source: ATEP Draft 03 sections 7 and 17, spec/schemas/atep.cddl; registry-endpoint is the seventh core claim type (Draft 05 section 7)
attestation-schema:
attestation = {
  subject: agent-id,
  issuer: agent-id,                      ; MUST equal the envelope signer
  claim: uri,
  data: { * tstr => any },
  ? evidence: bstr .size 32,
  ? evidence-uri: uri,
  id: bstr .size 16,
}
agent-id = bstr .size 32
uri = tstr

claims.name: domain-control
claims.title: Domain control
claims.summary: Subject is authorized for a DNS name, proven by a record at _atep.<domain> or https://<domain>/.well-known/atep.json.
description: The issuer states that it checked that the domain publishes the subject Agent ID, either in the document at https://<domain>/.well-known/atep.json or in a TXT record at _atep.<domain>. The protocol cannot verify that check, so monitors watch the log for domain-control attestations whose subject the domain owner does not recognize.
The binding applies to exactly the named DNS name. A binding for example.com does not bind a.example.com and the reverse; monitors that watch a name also watch every subdomain of it.
claims.subject: Agent ID of the identity the domain authorizes
claims.data-schema:
domain-control-data = { domain: dns-name, * tstr => any }
; lowercase DNS name: labels of 1 to 63 of a-z, 0-9 and "-" (no leading or
; trailing "-" in a label), at most 253 characters, no trailing dot.
dns-name = tstr
claims.data-checked-by: Logs at admission (schema_invalid); the core verifier does not check it.
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: operator
claims.title: Operator
claims.summary: Subject is operated by the named legal entity.
description: Names the legal entity (never a private individual, spec section 16 point 1) that operates the subject. Any issuer may make the statement; whether a verifier accepts it depends on its trust policy and the issuer's chain to a root.
The data map is free. The recommended layout is {"name": tstr}.
claims.issued-by: Any issuer (in ATEP-R, the fleet operator)
claims.subject: Agent ID operated by the entity
claims.data-schema: operator-data = { ? name: tstr, * tstr => any }   ; recommended layout, not enforced
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: successor
claims.title: Successor
claims.summary: Subject replaces the issuer's identity (key rotation).
description: Signed by the old identity, naming the new identity as subject. A verifier MAY follow exactly one hop of succession when no attestation of the old identity satisfies a rule for a signer that is the subject of a valid successor attestation. A second hop MUST NOT be followed and monitors SHOULD alert on it.
claims.subject: Agent ID of the new identity
claims.data-schema: successor-data = { ? reason: tstr, * tstr => any }   ; issuer is the old identity
claims.data-checked-by: The optional succession rule at step 9.
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: retired
claims.title: Retired
description: Self-issued: subject and issuer MUST be the same identity. It takes effect at its own issued-at. Afterwards any other envelope signed by that identity with an issued-at at or after the retirement MUST be rejected (step 8). No issuer can block or lift it (spec section 16 point 7).
claims.subject: The issuer's own Agent ID
claims.data-schema: retired-data = { ? reason: tstr, * tstr => any }   ; subject MUST equal issuer
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most; expiry is not compared when it is consulted at step 8

claims.name: issuer-authority
claims.title: Issuer authority
claims.summary: Subject may issue the listed claim types (chain delegation).
description: Delegates the right to issue the listed claim types. A verifier walks from a claim attestation up through issuer-authority attestations to a root in its trust policy. To let the subject delegate further, the list MUST contain the issuer-authority URI itself. An empty list delegates nothing. Delegation cannot exceed the delegator's own authority.
claims.issued-by: A root issuer or a delegate
claims.subject: Agent ID of the delegate
claims.data-schema:
issuer-authority-data = { claims: [* uri], * tstr => any }   ; REQUIRED layout
uri = tstr
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: audited
claims.title: Audited
claims.summary: Subject passed the named audit on the given date; evidence hash required.
description: The evidence field (SHA-256 of the audit report) is REQUIRED; every consumer rejects an audited attestation without it as attestation_schema_invalid. Because it carries evidence it is audit-backed and may live up to 400 days.
claims.subject: Agent ID that passed the audit
claims.data-schema:
audited-data = { ? audit: tstr, ? date: tstr, * tstr => any }   ; recommended layout, not enforced
; the attestation MUST carry evidence: bstr .size 32
claims.data-checked-by: Evidence presence by every consumer; the data map is not checked.

claims.name: robotics/fleet-member
claims.title: Fleet member
claims.summary: Subject belongs to the named fleet.
description: Minimum claim for ATEP-R telemetry and coordination commands, together with sensor-source for sensor data, and with peer-motion for delegated motion. Safety e-stops are accepted from a fleet-member that is also safety-certified.
claims.subject: Agent ID of the unit
claims.data-schema: fleet-member-data = { * tstr => any }   ; free map, recommended: fleet: tstr
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: robotics/fleet-controller
claims.title: Fleet controller
claims.summary: Subject may issue motion and coordination commands for the fleet.
description: Required for ATEP-R motion commands (or a fleet-member with a peer-motion delegation) and, together with safety-certified, for actuation commands.
claims.subject: Agent ID of the controller
claims.data-schema: fleet-controller-data = { * tstr => any }   ; free map, recommended: fleet: tstr
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: robotics/safety-certified
claims.title: Safety certified
claims.summary: Subject passed the named safety standard on the given date; evidence hash required.
description: Subject's software and hardware passed the named standard (for example ISO 10218, ISO 3691-4, UL 3100). The evidence field is REQUIRED. Together with fleet-controller it authorizes actuation; a fleet-member with safety-certified may send an e-stop.
claims.subject: Agent ID that passed
claims.data-schema:
safety-certified-data = { ? standard: tstr, ? date: tstr, * tstr => any }   ; recommended layout, not enforced
; the attestation MUST carry evidence: bstr .size 32
claims.data-checked-by: Evidence presence by every consumer; the data map is not checked.

claims.name: robotics/sensor-source
claims.title: Sensor source
claims.summary: Subject's named sensors are calibrated and trusted.
description: Required, together with fleet-member, for ATEP-R sensor commands (lidar, camera, detections).
claims.subject: Agent ID of the unit carrying the sensors
claims.data-schema: sensor-source-data = { * tstr => any }   ; free map, recommended: sensors: [* tstr]
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: robotics/safety-authority
claims.title: Safety authority
claims.summary: Subject may issue e-stops and geofence changes.
description: Required for ATEP-R safety commands other than an e-stop accepted from a safety-certified fleet-member.
claims.subject: Agent ID of the authority
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: robotics/maintenance-authority
claims.title: Maintenance authority
claims.summary: Subject may push firmware, configuration and key rotation.
description: Required for ATEP-R maintenance commands, which fail closed on a stale or missing revocation list.
claims.subject: Agent ID of the maintainer
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: robotics/peer-motion
claims.title: Peer motion
claims.summary: Subject may send motion commands to the listed peers.
description: Lets a fleet-member send motion commands to specific peers for cooperative tasks. The delegation counts for the ATEP-R motion class only when the receiving agent (the recipient identity that opened the envelope) is listed in data.peers; otherwise it fails with claim_data_mismatch.
In JSON tools an Agent ID in peers is written as {"$hex": "<64 hex characters>"}; on the wire it is a byte string of 32 bytes.
claims.subject: Agent ID allowed to command the peers
claims.data-schema:
peer-motion-data = { peers: [* agent-id], * tstr => any }   ; REQUIRED for the ATEP-R motion rule
agent-id = bstr .size 32
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most

claims.name: registry-endpoint
claims.title: Registry endpoint
claims.summary: Subject operates the service at the given URL (registry, verifier, MCP server or A2A agent).
description: Binds a service endpoint to an Agent ID through an ordinary attestation, so a client can find where an identity runs a registry, verifier, MCP server or A2A agent and check that the statement is logged. Attestations only: agent traffic is never logged (spec section 16 point 5).

kind is one of registry, verifier, mcp, a2a, or an extension name beginning with x-. A signed A2A agent card is carried by hashing the card JSON into the attestation evidence field and pointing evidence-uri at the card.

A log validates url (an https URL of at most 2048 characters with a host, no credentials and no whitespace) and kind at admission (schema_invalid); the core verifier does not check it. It is the seventh claim type of the core list of Draft 05, which with the seven robotics claim types makes 14.
claims.issued-by: The endpoint operator (usually the subject itself, or its domain owner)
claims.subject: Agent ID the endpoint belongs to
claims.data-checked-by: Logs at admission (schema_invalid); the core verifier does not check it.
claims.lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most
